question: "Tramline" bruising is a specific pattern caused by the impact of a cylindrical solid object. This would be classified as what type of bruise?

A patient with an abdominal aortic aneurysm has an atherosclerotic plaque with numerous activated macrophages. Which enzymes released by these cells contribute to degradation of the vascular extracellular matrix?
A patient arrives 2 hours after onset of severe chest pain coronary angiography demonstrates complete occlusion of an epicardial coronary artery. Which type of infarction is most likely?
A 45 year old women develops endothelial dysfunction associated with reduced nitic oxide availability. Which vascular function would be most directly impaired?

A 63-year-old woman who survived an acute transmural myocardial infarction 8 weeks ago attends a hospital-based outpatient cardiac rehabilitation program. The program features structured, medically supervised aerobic exercise training, nutritional counseling, psychosocial support, and optimization of secondary cardioprotective pharmacotherapy. This clinical intervention exemplifies which level of prevention?

Digoxin is a cardiac glycoside utilized in selected patients with heart failure and supraventricular arrhythmias because it enhances myocardial contractility while slowing atrioventricular (AV) nodal conduction through increased parasympathetic (vagal) activity. What is the fundamental molecular target directly inhibited by digoxin on the cardiomyocyte membrane?

A 58 year old man with hypertension and remote history of myocardial infarction with preserved left ventricular systolic function requires an additional antihypertensive agent. Immediate release short acting dihydropyridines (such as immediate-release nifedipine) are avoided because they cause reflex sympathetic tachycardia and increase myocardial oxygen demand. Which of the following calcium channel blockers exerts negative inotropic and chronotropic actions without triggering reflex tachycardia?

A 54-year-old man with a 6-year history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and mixed dyslipidemia is found to have microalbuminuria (urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 180 mg/g) on routine urinalysis. His current blood pressure is 152/92 mmHg. Which of the following antihypertensive medications is the preferred first-line agent due to its proven ability to reduce intraglomerular pressure and retard the progression of diabetic nephropathy
In medical jurisprudence and criminal law, how is the legal offense of 'assault' distinguished from 'battery'?

answers.option: Assault requires proof of actual bodily harm, whereas battery involves only non-contact verbal intimidation
Assault requires proof of severe permanent grievous injury, whereas battery is a minor bailable infraction
Assault cannot be legally committed without physical bodily contact simultaneously taking place
Assault involves an intentional act creating a reasonable apprehension of imminent harmful contact, whereas battery requires the actual unlawful application of physical force
Assault applies only to damage inflicted on tangible property, whereas battery applies to physical contact with a person

question: A patient with hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy develops worsening symptoms after standing suddenly. What is the likely mechanism?

answers.option: Reduced preload worsening LV outflow obstruction

question: A 26 year old women attends a pre-conceptional counseling clinic in anticipation of her first pregnancy. Which of the following nutritional supplements should be prescribed starting prior to conception and continued through out early pregnancy to significantly reduce the incidence of congenital anomalies, including congenital heart defects and neural tube defects?

In forensic traumatology, an abrasion that faithfully reproduces the distinctive geometrical pattern, weave, or surface configuration of the offending weapon or object upon the victim’s skin is termed an imprint or patterned abrasion.
Which of the following is a classic forensic example of an imprint abrasion?

answers.option: A curved crescentic scratch mark produced by a fingernail on the neck
An irregular linear scrape abrasion sustained during a slide over asphalt
An incised defense wound with cleanly divided tissue planes on the forearm
A stellate crush laceration over the vertex of the scalp
A grooved ligature mark around the neck bearing the weave pattern of a suspension rope in hanging

question: A provincial government introduces restrictions on tobacco advertising, requires healthier foods in schools and develops bicycle lanes to promote physical activity. Which preventive approach is best represented by these policies?
A patient develops myocardial infarction after prolonged hypotension due to septic shock. Only the inner one-third of the ventricular wall is involved. Which type of infarction is this?

A 4-year-old child with a known history of a large, uncorrected membranous ventricular septal defect (VSD) was previously noted to have a loud, harsh pansystolic murmur. Upon recent re-evaluation, the murmur has markedly softened and diminished in intensity, but the child has now developed perioral cyanosis on mild exertion and digital clubbing. What hemodynamic transition explains this clinical progression?

answers.option: Development of severe pulmonary vascular resistance leading to reversal of the shunt from right-to-left (Eisenmenger syndrome)
Acute infective endocarditis causing mitral valve leaflet perforation
Spontaneous anatomical closure of the ventricular septal defect with complete normalization of pressures
Development of isolated tricuspid valve insufficiency with right-sided heart failure
Development of acute left-to-right shunting through an acquired atrial septal defect

question: A 62-year-old man presents with facial plethora, periorbital edema, and prominent engorged superficial collateral veins over the anterior chest wall and neck. A contrast-enhanced chest CT scan confirms severe extrinsic compression and thrombosis of the superior vena cava by an invasive mediastinal mass. Which of the following neoplasms is the most common cause of superior vena cava (SVC) syndrome?

A 2-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department with a sudden episode of severe cyanosis and rapid breathing. His mother reports that similar episodes occur when he becomes upset or cries and that he often squats after playing. On examination, he is centrally cyanosed and has a harsh ejection systolic murmur at the left upper sternal border. Chest X-ray shows a normal-sized heart with reduced pulmonary vascular markings. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 67 year old man undergoes surgical internal fixation for an unstable pelvic fracture. On post operative day 3, following continuous strict bed rest, he develops unilateral calf swelling, warmth, tenderness and pitting edema. What component of Virchow's triad is the primary predisposing factor for this deep vein thrombosis (DVT)?

answers.option: venous stasis secondary to prolonged immobilization
Reactive thrombocytosis secondary to acute surgical blood loss
Direct mechanical transection of the popliteal vein
Increased lymphatic clearance and vascular compliance

question: A 66-year-old man who sustained an extensive anterior myocardial infarction remains persistently hypotensive with cold, clammy extremities, oliguria, and pulmonary vascular congestion despite initial intravenous fluid administration. What is the fundamental pathophysiological disturbance responsible for his cardiogenic shock?

answers.option: Severe primary myocardial pump failure resulting in critically reduced cardiac output and inadequate tissue perfusion
Severe intravascular volume depletion secondary to excessive osmotic diuresis
Capillary leak syndrome causing massive third-space fluid sequestration
Complete autonomic failure with loss of central sympathetic vasomotor tone
Widespread peripheral arteriolar vasodilation causing profound reduction in systemic vascular resistance

question: A 28-year-old woman presents with acute pleuritic chest pain following an upper respiratory tract infection. Cardiac examination reveals a three-phase pericardial friction rub. Which of the following electrocardiographic (ECG) patterns is characteristically seen during the early stage (Stage 1) of acute pericarditis?

answers.option: Focal convex ST-segment elevation with reciprocal ST-segment depression in opposite leads
Prominent S1Q3T3 pattern with right bundle branch block
Diffuse, widespread concave ST-segment elevation with PR-segment depression
Electrical alternans with alternating amplitude of the QRS complex in all leads
Deep pathological Q waves with symmetric T-wave inversions across leads II, III, and aVF

question: A 32-year-old man presents to the clinic with sharp, retrosternal chest pain that radiates to his left trapezius ridge. The pain is pleuritic, worsening significantly with coughing and deep inspiration. A high-pitched, scratchy friction rub is heard on auscultation. Which of the following positional changes is characteristically known to relieve the chest discomfort of acute pericarditis?

answers.option: Standing upright and performing the Valsalva maneuver
Flexing the knees and hips while lying supine
Lying flat in the supine position
Assuming the left lateral decubitus position

question: A pathologist examines an infarcted heart 5 days after myocardial infarction. Which cells are predominantly responsible for removal of dead myocardial fibers?

An elderly woman presents with a persistent, severe unilateral throbbing headache, scalp tenderness when brushing her hair, and pain in her jaw muscles while chewing. Laboratory evaluation reveals an ESR of 105 mm/hr and elevated C-reactive protein. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 16-year-old girl had acute rheumatic fever with carditis five years ago and now has mild residual mitral regurgitation. She comes in for a planned tooth extraction and has been faithfully receiving monthly benzathine penicillin prophylaxis. What is the best approach to take before the dental procedure?

answers.option: Temporarily stop her penicillin prophylaxis and use infective endocarditis prophylaxis in its place
Give only NSAIDs ahead of the procedure
Do not give prophylaxis of any type, because her residual valve disease is mild
Do not give any extra antibiotics, because her current penicillin prophylaxis already covers her
Add infective endocarditis prophylaxis on top of her ongoing secondary rheumatic fever prophylaxis

question: A 12-year-old girl is diagnosed with acute rheumatic fever after a throat infection. Which organism is the main trigger behind acute rheumatic fever and the chronic rheumatic heart disease that can follow?

A 10-year-old boy develops chorea, migratory polyarthritis, subcutaneous nodules, and a new apical holosystolic murmur three weeks after an untreated sore throat. The heart and valve damage in acute rheumatic fever results from antibody cross-reactivity aimed at which bacterial virulence factor?
A 54-year-old man with severe mitral regurgitation develops progressive dilation of the left ventricle. Which type of hypertrophy is most likely to occur?

An 18-year-old male basketball player suddenly collapses during strenuous exercise and dies despite resuscitation attempts. At autopsy, the heart shows disproportionate thickening of the interventricular septum compared with the left ventricular free wall, resulting in a narrowed, banana-shaped ventricular cavity. Which type of ventricular remodeling is most characteristic of this condition?

answers.option: Transmural ischemic wall thinning with aneurysm

question: A young adult man has a strong family history of dilated cardiomyopathy. Genetic testing identifies a truncating mutation in the TTN gene. Which protein is most directly affected by this mutation?
In ballistics, the internal bore of a rifled firearm barrel features alternating helical raised ridges and indented grooves. What is the primary mechanical and aerodynamic purpose of this rifling?

answers.option: Imparts rotational spin to the bullet around its longitudinal axis, improving flight stability and trajectory accuracy.
Reduces gas pressure within the barrel to prevent damage to the firearm chamber.
Dissipates excess heat to prevent barrel overheating during firing.
Decreases the muzzle velocity of the projectile to minimize terminal damage.
Facilitates the mechanical extraction and ejection of the spent cartridge case.

question: The likelihood and visibility of bruising following blunt trauma vary according to the tissue structure, skin thickness, and vascularity of the affected region. In which of the following anatomical sites is bruise formation most difficult or significantly delayed due to thick, tightly adherent skin and dense underlying fibrous tissue?

In traumatology, examining a blunt force injury requires differentiating between a contusion and laceration. Which of the following morphological characteristics fundamentally distinguishes a bruise from laceration?

answers.option: Tissue bridging of intact nerves and vessels occurs in a bruise but is absent in a  laceration
The anatomical continuity of the overlying skin remains intact in bruise
Extravasation of blood into the subcutaneous tissue occurs only in a laceration
Hair bulbs and nerve strands are cleanly sheared in a bruise
Wound margins are sharply incised, clean-cut, and everted in a bruise

question: Under the Qisas and Diyat law, an injury that does not involve the head or face and does not penetrate into a body cavity is classified as?
Shajjah-e-ammah is best defined as an injury to the head or face that:

answers.option: Penetrates into a body cavity of the trunk
Fractures the skull bone touching the membranes
Causes only superficial bleeding without exposing bone
Reaches the membrane of the brain without rupturing it
Exposes the bone without fracturing it

question: An elderly women with primary hypercholesterolemia is started on cholestyramine.  One month later, she presents with complain of severe bloating, abdominal fullness, and chronic constipation. Lab tests show mild decrease in fat-soluble vitamins. What is the primary mechanism of action of this medication?

answers.option: Direct chemical degradation of circulating chylomicrons
Binding and sequestration of bile acids in small intestine
Competitive inhibition of systemic triglyceride synthesis
Inactivation of intracellular hormone sensitive lipase
Upregulation of hepatic LDL receptors via PCSK9 inhibition

question: A patient develops hypotension, raised JVP and clear lung sounds after an inferior wall myocardial infraction. Which complication should be expected?

An elderly male is evaluated during routine follow-up appointment. He has been taking an antiarrhythmic drug for the past year to maintain sinus rhythm following a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. He reports recent progressive shortness of breath with exertion and a dry cough. A chest x-ray reveals patchy, bilateral interstitial infiltrates, restrictive pulmonary functionary tests. A 68 year old man undergoes an abdominal CT scan during an evaluation for persistent generalized back pain. The scan reveals a focal, asymmetrical outpouching involving only a portion of the abdominal aortic circumference on one side of the vessel wall, with a laminated mural thrombus occupying the lumen. A 62 year old women undergoes a vascular surgery. Few weeks later, she complains of a pulsatile mass at the side of arterial instrumentation. Imaging shows a defect in the arterial wall with an adjacent hematoma communicating with arterial lumen. What is the diagnosis?

answers.option: Ventricular septal rupture causing an acquired left to right

question: A 48-year-old man with a sedentary lifestyle and regular consumption of sugar-sweetened beverages visits his physician for a routine checkup. A 63-year-old patient with chronic stable angina is treated with both a beta-blocker and a long-acting nitrate.
